objects.description: Opaque CUDA stream handle typedef imported for interop with CUDA devices. It is a pointer to an incomplete struct from CUDA headers.
Opaque HIP stream handle typedef imported for interop with HIP devices. It is a pointer to an incomplete struct from HIP headers.
Objective-C-compatible typedef representing a Metal device object reference. When not compiling as Objective-C, it is a void* placeholder.
Objective-C-compatible typedef representing a Metal command queue object reference. When not compiling as Objective-C, it is a void* placeholder.
Objective-C-compatible typedef representing a Metal buffer object reference. When not compiling as Objective-C, it is a void* placeholder.
C enum of device types supported by Open Image Denoise. C++ alias exists as enum class oidn::DeviceType in oidn.hpp.
C enum of error codes returned by the API. C++ alias exists as enum class oidn::Error.

objects.definition: typedef void (*OIDNErrorFunction)(void* userPtr, OIDNError code, const char* message);
objects.description: Function pointer type for error callbacks receiving user data, an error code, and a message.
Opaque handle to a device object. Reference-counted via oidnRetainDevice/oidnReleaseDevice and configured/used via device APIs.

objects.definition:

objects.description: C enum of buffer/image pixel formats supported by the API. C++ alias exists as enum class oidn::Format.
C enum of buffer storage location/mode. C++ alias exists as enum class oidn::Storage.

{

objects.description: Bitmask-style C enum describing external memory handle types for shared buffers. C++ aliases exist as enum class oidn::ExternalMemoryTypeFlag and Flags wrapper oidn::ExternalMemoryTypeFlags.
Opaque handle to a buffer object owned by the device. Reference-counted via oidnRetainBuffer/oidnReleaseBuffer. Created by buffer creation functions and used for image/data storage.
C enum of filter quality/performance presets. C++ alias exists as enum class oidn::Quality.
Function pointer type for progress monitoring callbacks; returning false may cancel execution.
Opaque handle to a filter object. Reference-counted via oidnRetainFilter/oidnReleaseFilter. Configured with images/parameters then committed and executed.

functions.name: oidnGetNumPhysicalDevices
functions.signature: OIDN_API int oidnGetNumPhysicalDevices();
functions.description: Returns the number of supported physical devices detected by Open Image Denoise. Use the returned count to iterate valid physicalDeviceID values for subsequent physical-device queries or device creation.
requirements: May be called without creating any device.

functions.name: oidnGetPhysicalDeviceBool
functions.signature: OIDN_API bool oidnGetPhysicalDeviceBool(int physicalDeviceID, const char* name);
functions.description: Gets a boolean parameter of a physical device by ID. The specific parameter is selected by the name string (e.g., feature flags).
requirements: physicalDeviceID must be in the range [0, oidnGetNumPhysicalDevices()-1].
name must be a valid parameter name recognized by the library.
May be called with no device created.

functions.name: oidnGetPhysicalDeviceInt
functions.signature: OIDN_API int oidnGetPhysicalDeviceInt(int physicalDeviceID, const char* name);
functions.description: Gets an integer parameter of a physical device by ID. Parameter is chosen by string name.
requirements: physicalDeviceID must be in the range [0, oidnGetNumPhysicalDevices()-1].
name must be a valid parameter name recognized by the library.
May be called with no device created.

functions.name: oidnGetPhysicalDeviceUInt
functions.signature: inline unsigned int oidnGetPhysicalDeviceUInt(int physicalDeviceID, const char* name)
functions.description: Convenience inline wrapper that returns an unsigned integer physical device parameter by casting the result of oidnGetPhysicalDeviceInt.
requirements: physicalDeviceID must be in the range [0, oidnGetNumPhysicalDevices()-1].
name must be a valid parameter name recognized by the library.
May be called with no device created.

functions.name: oidnGetPhysicalDeviceString
functions.signature: OIDN_API const char* oidnGetPhysicalDeviceString(int physicalDeviceID, const char* name);
functions.description: Gets a string parameter of a physical device by ID. The returned C string is owned by the library.
requirements: physicalDeviceID must be in the range [0, oidnGetNumPhysicalDevices()-1].
name must be a valid parameter name recognized by the library.
Caller must not attempt to free or modify the returned string.
May be called with no device created.

functions.name: oidnGetPhysicalDeviceData
functions.signature: OIDN_API const void* oidnGetPhysicalDeviceData(int physicalDeviceID, const char* name, size_t* byteSize);
functions.description: Gets an opaque data parameter of a physical device by ID, returning a pointer and its size via byteSize. The memory is owned by the library.
requirements: physicalDeviceID must be in the range [0, oidnGetNumPhysicalDevices()-1].
name must be a valid parameter name recognized by the library.
byteSize must be non-null if the caller needs the size; if non-null it will be set by the function.
Caller must not free or modify the returned memory.
May be called with no device created.

functions.name: oidnIsCPUDeviceSupported
functions.signature: OIDN_API bool oidnIsCPUDeviceSupported();
functions.description: Returns whether the CPU device backend is supported on the current system.

functions.name: oidnIsSYCLDeviceSupported
functions.signature: OIDN_API bool oidnIsSYCLDeviceSupported(const sycl::device* device);
functions.description: Returns whether the specified SYCL device is supported by Open Image Denoise.
requirements: Only available when compiling as C++ with SYCL types visible.
device must be a valid pointer to a sycl::device object.

functions.name: oidnIsCUDADeviceSupported
functions.signature: OIDN_API bool oidnIsCUDADeviceSupported(int deviceID);
functions.description: Returns whether the specified CUDA device (by CUDA device ID) is supported.
requirements: deviceID must refer to an existing CUDA device on the system.

functions.name: oidnIsHIPDeviceSupported
functions.signature: OIDN_API bool oidnIsHIPDeviceSupported(int deviceID);
functions.description: Returns whether the specified HIP device (by HIP device ID) is supported.
requirements: deviceID must refer to an existing HIP device on the system.

functions.name: oidnIsMetalDeviceSupported
functions.signature: OIDN_API bool oidnIsMetalDeviceSupported(MTLDevice_id device);
functions.description: Returns whether the specified Metal device is supported.
requirements: device must be a valid Metal MTLDevice object reference.

functions.name: oidnNewDevice
functions.signature: OIDN_API OIDNDevice oidnNewDevice(OIDNDeviceType type);
functions.description: Creates a new device of the specified backend type (e.g., default, CPU, SYCL, CUDA, HIP, Metal). Returns a device handle or null on failure.
requirements: type must be a valid OIDNDeviceType supported on the system.
On failure, error can be queried via oidnGetDeviceError(nullptr, ...).
Caller must call oidnReleaseDevice when done with the device.
Caller must call oidnCommitDevice before first using the device (e.g., creating filters).

functions.name: oidnNewDeviceByID
functions.signature: OIDN_API OIDNDevice oidnNewDeviceByID(int physicalDeviceID);
functions.description: Creates a device from a physical device specified by its enumerated ID.
requirements: physicalDeviceID must be in [0, oidnGetNumPhysicalDevices()-1].
On failure, error can be queried via oidnGetDeviceError(nullptr, ...).
Caller must release the returned device with oidnReleaseDevice.
Caller must call oidnCommitDevice before first using the device.

functions.name: oidnNewDeviceByUUID
functions.signature: OIDN_API OIDNDevice oidnNewDeviceByUUID(const void* uuid);
functions.description: Creates a device from a physical device specified by its UUID byte array.
requirements: uuid must point to a buffer of size OIDN_UUID_SIZE bytes.
On failure, error can be queried via oidnGetDeviceError(nullptr, ...).
Caller must release the returned device with oidnReleaseDevice.
Caller must call oidnCommitDevice before first using the device.

functions.name: oidnNewDeviceByLUID
functions.signature: OIDN_API OIDNDevice oidnNewDeviceByLUID(const void* luid);
functions.description: Creates a device from a physical device specified by its LUID byte array.
requirements: luid must point to a buffer of size OIDN_LUID_SIZE bytes.
On failure, error can be queried via oidnGetDeviceError(nullptr, ...).
Caller must release the returned device with oidnReleaseDevice.
Caller must call oidnCommitDevice before first using the device.

functions.name: oidnNewDeviceByPCIAddress
functions.signature: OIDN_API OIDNDevice oidnNewDeviceByPCIAddress(int pciDomain, int pciBus, int pciDevice, int pciFunction);
functions.description: Creates a device from a physical device specified by its PCI address (domain, bus, device, function).
requirements: pciDomain, pciBus, pciDevice, pciFunction must identify a supported device.
On failure, error can be queried via oidnGetDeviceError(nullptr, ...).
Caller must release the returned device with oidnReleaseDevice.
Caller must call oidnCommitDevice before first using the device.

functions.name: oidnNewSYCLDevice
functions.signature: OIDN_API OIDNDevice oidnNewSYCLDevice(const sycl::queue* queues, int numQueues);
functions.description: Creates a device from a list of SYCL queues. Intended for multi-tile/sub-device configurations.
requirements: Only available when compiling as C++ with SYCL types visible.
queues must point to an array of numQueues valid sycl::queue objects.
numQueues must be >= 1.
The queues should belong to different SYCL sub-devices (Xe Stack/Tile) of the same SYCL root-device (GPU).
Caller must release the returned device with oidnReleaseDevice.
Caller must call oidnCommitDevice before first using the device.

functions.name: oidnNewCUDADevice
functions.signature: OIDN_API OIDNDevice oidnNewCUDADevice(const int* deviceIDs, const cudaStream_t* streams, int numPairs);
functions.description: Creates a device from pairs of CUDA device IDs and streams (null stream = default stream). Currently supports only one pair.
requirements: deviceIDs must point to an array of length numPairs containing CUDA device IDs.
streams must point to an array of length numPairs containing CUDA streams (may include null).
numPairs must be >= 1. Currently only one device ID/stream is supported.
Caller must release the returned device with oidnReleaseDevice.
Caller must call oidnCommitDevice before first using the device.

functions.name: oidnNewHIPDevice
functions.signature: OIDN_API OIDNDevice oidnNewHIPDevice(const int* deviceIDs, const hipStream_t* streams, int numPairs);
functions.description: Creates a device from pairs of HIP device IDs and streams (null stream = default stream). Currently supports only one pair.
requirements: deviceIDs must point to an array of length numPairs containing HIP device IDs.
streams must point to an array of length numPairs containing HIP streams (may include null).
numPairs must be >= 1. Currently only one device ID/stream is supported.
Caller must release the returned device with oidnReleaseDevice.
Caller must call oidnCommitDevice before first using the device.

functions.name: oidnNewMetalDevice
functions.signature: OIDN_API OIDNDevice oidnNewMetalDevice(const MTLCommandQueue_id* commandQueues, int numQueues);
functions.description: Creates a device from a list of Metal command queues. Currently only one queue is supported.
requirements: commandQueues must point to an array of length numQueues containing valid Metal command queues.
numQueues must be >= 1. Currently only one queue is supported.
Caller must release the returned device with oidnReleaseDevice.
Caller must call oidnCommitDevice before first using the device.

functions.name: oidnRetainDevice
functions.signature: OIDN_API void oidnRetainDevice(OIDNDevice device);
functions.description: Increments the reference count of a device handle.
requirements: device must be a valid device handle previously created by the API.

functions.name: oidnReleaseDevice
functions.signature: OIDN_API void oidnReleaseDevice(OIDNDevice device);
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of a device handle; destroys the device when the count reaches zero.
requirements: device must be a valid device handle (may be null in some implementations, but not stated).
After release that drops the last reference, the handle must not be used again.

functions.name: oidnSetDeviceBool
functions.signature: OIDN_API void oidnSetDeviceBool(OIDNDevice device, const char* name, bool value);
functions.description: Sets a boolean parameter on the given device by name.
requirements: device must be a valid device handle.
name must be a recognized device parameter.
Call oidnCommitDevice to apply changes before first use.

functions.name: oidnSetDevice1b
functions.signature: inline void oidnSetDevice1b(OIDNDevice device, const char* name, bool value)
functions.description: Deprecated alias of oidnSetDeviceBool. Forwards to oidnSetDeviceBool.
requirements: device must be a valid device handle.
name must be a recognized device parameter.
Call oidnCommitDevice to apply changes before first use.

functions.name: oidnSetDeviceInt
functions.signature: OIDN_API void oidnSetDeviceInt(OIDNDevice device, const char* name, int value);
functions.description: Sets an integer parameter on the given device by name.
requirements: device must be a valid device handle.
name must be a recognized device parameter.
Call oidnCommitDevice to apply changes before first use.

functions.name: oidnSetDevice1i
functions.signature: inline void oidnSetDevice1i(OIDNDevice device, const char* name, int value)
functions.description: Deprecated alias of oidnSetDeviceInt. Forwards to oidnSetDeviceInt.
requirements: device must be a valid device handle.
name must be a recognized device parameter.
Call oidnCommitDevice to apply changes before first use.

functions.name: oidnSetDeviceUInt
functions.signature: inline void oidnSetDeviceUInt(OIDNDevice device, const char* name, unsigned int value)
functions.description: Convenience inline wrapper that sets an unsigned integer device parameter by forwarding to oidnSetDeviceInt with cast.
requirements: device must be a valid device handle.
name must be a recognized device parameter.
Call oidnCommitDevice to apply changes before first use.

functions.name: oidnGetDeviceBool
functions.signature: OIDN_API bool oidnGetDeviceBool(OIDNDevice device, const char* name);
functions.description: Gets a boolean parameter of the device by name.
requirements: device must be a valid device handle.
name must be a recognized device parameter.

functions.name: oidnGetDevice1b
functions.signature: inline bool oidnGetDevice1b(OIDNDevice device, const char* name)
functions.description: Deprecated alias of oidnGetDeviceBool. Forwards to oidnGetDeviceBool.
requirements: device must be a valid device handle.
name must be a recognized device parameter.

functions.name: oidnGetDeviceInt
functions.signature: OIDN_API int oidnGetDeviceInt(OIDNDevice device, const char* name);
functions.description: Gets an integer parameter of the device by name.
requirements: device must be a valid device handle.
name must be a recognized device parameter.

functions.name: oidnGetDeviceUInt
functions.signature: inline unsigned int oidnGetDeviceUInt(OIDNDevice device, const char* name)
functions.description: Convenience inline wrapper that returns an unsigned integer device parameter by casting the result of oidnGetDeviceInt.
requirements: device must be a valid device handle.
name must be a recognized device parameter.

functions.name: oidnGetDevice1i
functions.signature: inline int oidnGetDevice1i(OIDNDevice device, const char* name)
functions.description: Deprecated alias of oidnGetDeviceInt. Forwards to oidnGetDeviceInt.
requirements: device must be a valid device handle.
name must be a recognized device parameter.

functions.name: oidnSetDeviceErrorFunction
functions.signature: OIDN_API void oidnSetDeviceErrorFunction(OIDNDevice device, OIDNErrorFunction func, void* userPtr);
functions.description: Registers an error callback function for the device. The callback receives a user pointer, error code, and message when errors occur.
requirements: device must be a valid device handle (may be null not stated).
func may be null to clear the callback (not explicitly stated; behavior unknown).
The callback must be thread-safe if used across threads.

functions.name: oidnGetDeviceError
functions.signature: OIDN_API OIDNError oidnGetDeviceError(OIDNDevice device, const char** outMessage);
functions.description: Returns and clears the first unqueried error code stored in the device for the current thread, optionally returns a message string. Can be called with a null device to check per-thread global errors.
requirements: outMessage may be null; if non-null and an error exists, it will be set to a message string owned by the library.
May be called with device = NULL to retrieve global errors (e.g., about device creation or physical device queries).
Returned message pointer must not be freed or modified by the caller.

functions.name: oidnCommitDevice
functions.signature: OIDN_API void oidnCommitDevice(OIDNDevice device);
functions.description: Commits all previous parameter changes to the device. Must be called before first using the device (e.g., creating filters).
requirements: device must be a valid device handle.
Must be called before first using the device (e.g., creating filters).

functions.name: oidnSyncDevice
functions.signature: OIDN_API void oidnSyncDevice(OIDNDevice device);
functions.description: Blocks until all asynchronous operations running on the device complete.
requirements: device must be a valid device handle.

functions.name: oidnNewBuffer
functions.signature: OIDN_API OIDNBuffer oidnNewBuffer(OIDNDevice device, size_t byteSize);
functions.description: Creates a new buffer accessible to both the host and device with the specified size in bytes.
requirements: device must be a valid committed device.
byteSize specifies the buffer size; 0 creates an empty buffer (behavior for 0 inferred; not explicitly stated).
Caller must release the returned buffer with oidnReleaseBuffer.

functions.name: oidnNewBufferWithStorage
functions.signature: OIDN_API OIDNBuffer oidnNewBufferWithStorage(OIDNDevice device, size_t byteSize, OIDNStorage storage);
functions.description: Creates a new buffer with the specified storage mode (host, device, or managed).
requirements: device must be a valid committed device.
storage must be a supported OIDNStorage for the device (managed memory support must be checked via device parameter if used).
Caller must release the returned buffer with oidnReleaseBuffer.

functions.name: oidnNewSharedBuffer
functions.signature: OIDN_API OIDNBuffer oidnNewSharedBuffer(OIDNDevice device, void* devPtr, size_t byteSize);
functions.description: Creates a shared buffer from memory allocated and owned by the user that is accessible to the device.
requirements: device must be a valid committed device.
devPtr must point to device-accessible memory for the target backend.
byteSize must match the size of the memory region provided.
Caller must keep the underlying memory alive for the lifetime of the buffer handle.
Caller must release the returned buffer with oidnReleaseBuffer.

functions.name: oidnNewSharedBufferFromFD
functions.signature: OIDN_API OIDNBuffer oidnNewSharedBufferFromFD(OIDNDevice device, OIDNExternalMemoryTypeFlag fdType, int fd, size_t byteSize);
functions.description: Creates a shared buffer by importing external memory from a POSIX file descriptor of a specified external memory type.
requirements: device must be a valid committed device.
fdType must be an appropriate external memory type for the given fd (e.g., OpaqueFD or DMABuf).
fd must be a valid file descriptor referring to exportable memory.
byteSize must match the memory size being imported.
Ownership/duplication semantics of fd are library-defined; caller should not close fd until import rules allow (details not specified).
Caller must release the returned buffer with oidnReleaseBuffer.

functions.name: oidnNewSharedBufferFromWin32Handle
functions.signature: OIDN_API OIDNBuffer oidnNewSharedBufferFromWin32Handle(OIDNDevice device, OIDNExternalMemoryTypeFlag handleType, void* handle, const void* name, size_t byteSize);
functions.description: Creates a shared buffer by importing external memory from a Win32 handle of a specified external memory type.
requirements: device must be a valid committed device.
handleType must match the handle (e.g., OpaqueWin32, D3D11/12 resource/heap types).
handle must be a valid Win32 handle to exportable memory/resource.
name is used with some handle types (may be null depending on type; behavior not specified).
byteSize must match the memory size being imported.
Caller must release the returned buffer with oidnReleaseBuffer.

functions.name: oidnNewSharedBufferFromMetal
functions.signature: OIDN_API OIDNBuffer oidnNewSharedBufferFromMetal(OIDNDevice device, MTLBuffer_id buffer);
functions.description: Creates a shared buffer from a Metal MTLBuffer.
requirements: device must be a valid committed device.
buffer must be a valid MTLBuffer.
Only Metal buffers with shared or private storage and hazard tracking are supported.
Caller must release the returned buffer with oidnReleaseBuffer.

functions.name: oidnGetBufferSize
functions.signature: OIDN_API size_t oidnGetBufferSize(OIDNBuffer buffer);
functions.description: Returns the size of the buffer in bytes.
requirements: buffer must be a valid buffer handle.

functions.name: oidnGetBufferStorage
functions.signature: OIDN_API OIDNStorage oidnGetBufferStorage(OIDNBuffer buffer);
functions.description: Returns the storage mode of the buffer (host, device, or managed).
requirements: buffer must be a valid buffer handle.

functions.name: oidnGetBufferData
functions.signature: OIDN_API void* oidnGetBufferData(OIDNBuffer buffer);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the buffer data. The pointer is accessible to the device but may not be host-accessible depending on the storage mode. May return null if the buffer is empty or device storage pointer retrieval is not supported.
requirements: buffer must be a valid buffer handle.
Caller must not assume host access if storage is device-only.

functions.name: oidnReadBuffer
functions.signature: OIDN_API void oidnReadBuffer(OIDNBuffer buffer, size_t byteOffset, size_t byteSize, void* dstHostPtr);
functions.description: Copies data from a region of the buffer into host memory synchronously.
requirements: buffer must be a valid buffer handle.
dstHostPtr must point to a host-accessible destination buffer of at least byteSize bytes.
byteOffset and byteSize must specify a range within the buffer.

functions.name: oidnReadBufferAsync
functions.signature: OIDN_API void oidnReadBufferAsync(OIDNBuffer buffer, size_t byteOffset, size_t byteSize, void* dstHostPtr);
functions.description: Asynchronously copies data from a region of the buffer into host memory.
requirements: buffer must be a valid buffer handle.
dstHostPtr must point to a host-accessible destination buffer of at least byteSize bytes.
byteOffset and byteSize must specify a range within the buffer.
Caller may need to synchronize via oidnSyncDevice or other mechanism before reusing dstHostPtr.

functions.name: oidnWriteBuffer
functions.signature: OIDN_API void oidnWriteBuffer(OIDNBuffer buffer, size_t byteOffset, size_t byteSize, const void* srcHostPtr);
functions.description: Copies data from host memory into a region of the buffer synchronously.
requirements: buffer must be a valid buffer handle.
srcHostPtr must point to at least byteSize bytes of host memory.
byteOffset and byteSize must specify a range within the buffer.

functions.name: oidnWriteBufferAsync
functions.signature: OIDN_API void oidnWriteBufferAsync(OIDNBuffer buffer, size_t byteOffset, size_t byteSize, const void* srcHostPtr);
functions.description: Asynchronously copies data from host memory into a region of the buffer.
requirements: buffer must be a valid buffer handle.
srcHostPtr must point to at least byteSize bytes of host memory.
byteOffset and byteSize must specify a range within the buffer.
Caller may need to synchronize via oidnSyncDevice or other mechanism before reusing or freeing srcHostPtr.

functions.name: oidnRetainBuffer
functions.signature: OIDN_API void oidnRetainBuffer(OIDNBuffer buffer);
functions.description: Increments the reference count of a buffer handle.
requirements: buffer must be a valid buffer handle.

functions.name: oidnReleaseBuffer
functions.signature: OIDN_API void oidnReleaseBuffer(OIDNBuffer buffer);
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of a buffer handle; destroys the buffer when the count reaches zero.
requirements: buffer must be a valid buffer handle.
After release that drops the last reference, the handle must not be used again.

functions.name: oidnNewFilter
functions.signature: OIDN_API OIDNFilter oidnNewFilter(OIDNDevice device, const char* type);
functions.description: Creates a filter of the specified type (e.g., "RT"). Returns a filter handle or null on failure.
requirements: device must be a valid committed device.
type must be a recognized filter type string for the device/backend.
Caller must release the returned filter with oidnReleaseFilter.
Caller must call oidnCommitFilter before first executing the filter.

functions.name: oidnRetainFilter
functions.signature: OIDN_API void oidnRetainFilter(OIDNFilter filter);
functions.description: Increments the reference count of a filter handle.
requirements: filter must be a valid filter handle.

functions.name: oidnReleaseFilter
functions.signature: OIDN_API void oidnReleaseFilter(OIDNFilter filter);
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of a filter handle; destroys the filter when the count reaches zero.
requirements: filter must be a valid filter handle.
After release that drops the last reference, the handle must not be used again.

functions.name: oidnSetFilterImage
functions.signature: OIDN_API void oidnSetFilterImage(OIDNFilter filter, const char* name, OIDNBuffer buffer, OIDNFormat format, size_t width, size_t height, size_t byteOffset, size_t pixelByteStride, size_t rowByteStride);
functions.description: Sets an image parameter of the filter using data stored in a buffer. Strides of 0 are computed automatically.
requirements: filter must be a valid filter handle.
buffer must be a valid buffer containing the image data.
format must be an OIDNFormat matching the buffer data layout.
width and height specify image dimensions; must be consistent with buffer size.
If pixelByteStride or rowByteStride is 0, they will be computed automatically.
Call oidnCommitFilter before executing the filter.

functions.name: oidnSetSharedFilterImage
functions.signature: OIDN_API void oidnSetSharedFilterImage(OIDNFilter filter, const char* name, void* devPtr, OIDNFormat format, size_t width, size_t height, size_t byteOffset, size_t pixelByteStride, size_t rowByteStride);
functions.description: Sets an image parameter of the filter using user-owned memory accessible to the device. Strides of 0 are computed automatically.
requirements: filter must be a valid filter handle.
devPtr must point to device-accessible image memory with the specified layout.
format must be an OIDNFormat matching the memory layout.
width and height specify image dimensions; must be consistent with provided memory region.
If pixelByteStride or rowByteStride is 0, they will be computed automatically.
Caller must keep the memory alive and unchanged (unless allowed) while the filter may read it.
Call oidnCommitFilter before executing the filter.

functions.name: oidnUnsetFilterImage
functions.signature: OIDN_API void oidnUnsetFilterImage(OIDNFilter filter, const char* name);
functions.description: Unsets a previously set image parameter of the filter by name.
requirements: filter must be a valid filter handle.
name must refer to an image parameter previously set or recognized by the filter.

functions.name: oidnRemoveFilterImage
functions.signature: inline void oidnRemoveFilterImage(OIDNFilter filter, const char* name)
functions.description: Deprecated alias of oidnUnsetFilterImage. Forwards to oidnUnsetFilterImage.
requirements: filter must be a valid filter handle.
name must refer to an image parameter previously set or recognized by the filter.

functions.name: oidnSetSharedFilterData
functions.signature: OIDN_API void oidnSetSharedFilterData(OIDNFilter filter, const char* name, void* hostPtr, size_t byteSize);
functions.description: Sets an opaque data parameter of the filter using user-owned host memory.

data_types.description: A generic ASCII/UTF-8 string used to select a named parameter or property in the API (e.g., "type", "name", "vendor", "uuid", "luid", "color", "albedo", "normal", "output", "verbose", "numThreads", "weights", "scratch", "state"). The string must match one of the names recognized by the library; otherwise the call reports an error.

An uninterpreted byte buffer of any length containing arbitrary data. Used as generic input payloads for buffer writes or opaque/shared data parameters. No specific encoding or structure is required; bytes are consumed as-is.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Generator for valid/interesting parameter name strings used by OIDN stubs.
# We aim to return bytes containing a single ASCII/UTF-8 string. The fuzzing
# harness will consume this buffer as FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and as filenames if needed.
# We bias towards known-good names used in the stubs and API, and add variety via
# random casing, separators, and mixed lists separated by NULs or newlines.

_KNOWN_DEVICE_QUERY_NAMES = [
    # Physical device/property queries
    "type", "name", "vendor", "driver", "backend", "uuid", "luid",
]

_KNOWN_FILTER_IMAGE_NAMES = [
    "color", "albedo", "normal", "output",
]

_KNOWN_DEVICE_PARAM_NAMES = [
    "affinity", "setAffinity", "verbose", "numThreads",
]

_KNOWN_FILTER_BOOL_NAMES = [
    "hdr", "srgb", "cleanAux",
]

_KNOWN_FILTER_INT_NAMES = [
    "maxMemoryMB", "quality",
]

_KNOWN_FILTER_FLOAT_NAMES = [
    "hdrScale", "inputScale",
]

_KNOWN_DATA_PARAM_NAMES = [
    "weights", "scratch", "state",
]

# Weighted pools tailored to the various stubs, increasing chance of recognized names
_POOLS: List[List[str]] = [
    _KNOWN_DEVICE_QUERY_NAMES,
    _KNOWN_FILTER_IMAGE_NAMES,
    _KNOWN_DEVICE_PARAM_NAMES,
    _KNOWN_FILTER_BOOL_NAMES,
    _KNOWN_FILTER_INT_NAMES,
    _KNOWN_FILTER_FLOAT_NAMES,
    _KNOWN_DATA_PARAM_NAMES,
]

# Utility to vary casing and add subtle, still-valid variants commonly accepted by APIs.
def _case_variants(s: str, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    mode = rng.randint(0, 4)
    if mode == 0:
        return s
    if mode == 1:
        return s.upper()
    if mode == 2:
        return s.capitalize()
    if mode == 3:
        # random per-character case
        return "".join(c.upper() if rng.getrandbits(1) else c.lower() for c in s)
    # mode 4: add benign surrounding whitespace (often trimmed by APIs)
    return (" " * rng.randint(0, 1)) + s + (" " * rng.randint(0, 1))

# Compose multiple parameter names in one buffer separated by NUL/newline to
# provide multiple interesting FUZZ_PARAM_STR() pulls from the same buffer.
# The harness typically returns one string per call, but supplying multiple
# concatenated strings increases coverage for subsequent calls.

def _compose_buffer(strings: List[str], rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose a separator strategy
    sep_mode = rng.randint(0, 3)
    if sep_mode == 0:
        sep = "\0"  # NUL-separated
    elif sep_mode == 1:
        sep = "\n"  # newline-separated
    elif sep_mode == 2:
        sep = "\r\n"  # Windows-style newline
    else:
        # mixed separators
        seps = ["\0", "\n", "\r\n"]
        parts = []
        for i, s in enumerate(strings):
            parts.append(s)
            if i + 1 < len(strings):
                parts.append(seps[rng.randrange(len(seps))])
        return ("".join(parts)).encode("utf-8")
    return sep.join(strings).encode("utf-8")

# Add a few synthetic entries commonly seen in real configs but still valid
# names for this API set, to trigger different code paths that accept synonyms
# or extended properties.
_EXTRA_NAMES = [
    "device", "backend", "RT", "RTLightmap", "RTRef"
]

# Ensure result size remains within 4096 bytes.
_MAX_SIZE = 4096


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a basket of names, heavily favoring known-good names but with some noise.
    basket: List[str] = []

    # Select several pools to ensure variety across different stubs.
    pool_order = list(range(len(_POOLS)))
    rng.shuffle(pool_order)

    # For each selected pool, pick 1-3 entries with case variants.
    for idx in pool_order:
        pool = _POOLS[idx]
        count = 1 + rng.randint(0, 2)
        choices = rng.sample(pool, k=min(count, len(pool)))
        for c in choices:
            basket.append(_case_variants(c, rng))

    # Add some duplicates and alternates to help stubs expecting specific names.
    # Include canonical lowercase to maximize validity.
    canonical = [
        "type", "name", "vendor", "uuid", "luid",
        "color", "albedo", "normal", "output",
        "verbose", "numThreads",
        "weights", "scratch", "state",
        "hdr", "srgb", "cleanAux",
        "maxMemoryMB", "quality",
        "hdrScale", "inputScale",
    ]
    # Deterministically choose a subset size
    extra_count = 5 + rng.randint(0, 8)
    basket.extend(rng.sample(canonical, k=min(extra_count, len(canonical))))

    # Sprinkle a few extras and harmless whitespace-padded variants
    extras = rng.sample(_EXTRA_NAMES, k=min(2, len(_EXTRA_NAMES)))
    basket.extend(_case_variants(e, rng) for e in extras)

    # Guarantee presence of names that some stubs prefer first
    for must in ("type", "name", "uuid", "luid", "color", "output"):
        if must not in basket:
            basket.append(must)

    # Compose into a buffer with separators, ensuring we do not exceed _MAX_SIZE.
    rng.shuffle(basket)

    # Iteratively add strings until we approach the limit.
    out_strings: List[str] = []
    # Prepend a short length header in ASCII to help parsers that read a size first,
    # but keep it purely textual so FUZZ_PARAM_STR can still parse names seamlessly.
    header = f"{len(basket)}\n"
    current = header.encode("utf-8")

    for s in basket:
        candidate = _compose_buffer(out_strings + [s], rng)
        buf = header.encode("utf-8") + candidate
        if len(buf) > _MAX_SIZE:
            break
        out_strings.append(s)
        current = buf

    # Ensure buffer ends with a terminator suitable for C-strings extraction
    # without forcing the harness; append a NUL if not already present.
    if not current.endswith(b"\0"):
        if len(current) + 1 <= _MAX_SIZE:
            current += b"\0"

    return current
